correctness.rationale: The cubic outside-vertex two-colour neighbourhood condition is exactly equivalent to the 16-state cyclic transfer. Two polynomial determinants were symbolically reconstructed from the actual transition rules. The substitution z=t^2, x=u/t yields no negative defect powers and exact rational identities for all low-degree coefficients, proving each four-residue minimum count and the single six-rung exception. A second transfer for unrestricted domination proves the 2n difference. Primitive strongly connected transition graphs and Perron-Frobenius prove exponential ratio. A standalone checker exhaustively compares actual subsets for 3<=n<=9 and exact formula through n=30; these finite tests are only supplemental.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Restrained domination is equivalent to requiring each unselected cubic vertex to have between one and two selected neighbors. This differs from ordinary domination (one or more), total restrained domination (also constraining selected vertices), and one-limited domination (a different condition on selected vertices). The available exact prism papers did not state a matching restrained all-cardinality polynomial.

value.rationale: The result determines all guard-set sizes in an established cubic prism family rather than a routine minimum bound. It proves a quantified 2n class of otherwise-optimal but nonrestrained guards, a four-residue optimum multiplicity law with a genuine n=6 exception, and an exponential rarity rate about 0.854312^n despite identical optimizing cardinalities. These are structurally motivated distributional facts useful for comparing nominal and restrained placements.
